newsitem.title: USA: Washington Gov. vetoes part of $19 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: Washington Gov. vetoes part of $19 bln budget.

text.p: Washington Gov. Gary Locke on Wednesday vetoed major sections of the state legislature's $19 billion budget proposal and called on lawmakers to craft a plan providing more education and health care funding.
Locke's veto forced the Republican-controlled state legislature back into budget negotiations as the legislative session was coming to an end.
Republican lawmakers said, however, that they should be able to make budget adjustments to satisfy the Democratic governor before their session ends on Sunday.
The state legislature's $19 billion budget proposal was approved by the Republican-dominated Senate after a heated weekend battle with Democrats.
The two-year spending plan included about $400 million in tax cuts and called for a record state budget reserve of about $500 million.
Democrats in the legislature said the budget would not do enough to help financially-strapped school districts, workers needing job retraining, and people without health insurance.
Locke said his "constructive vetoes" were designed to focus the attention of lawmakers on these issues.
In a statement, Locke urged lawmakers to provide additional support for public education, health care, job training and water resources.

"I understand the need for compromise but I don't think the state's interests are served by short-changing education and programs that help working families when we have the resources to support those services and still leave a prudent reserve," Locke said in a statement.
Locke's budget proposal called for a $300 million reserve.
